own_scenes.place: El Bronx y Lower East Side (East River Park)
own_scenes.desc: Charlie Ahearn conoció a Fab 5 Freddy en el Times Square Show (1980) y juntos idearon Wild Style (1982), con los cuatro elementos: los grafiteros Lee Quiñones y Lady Pink, Freddy como el promotor Phade, Flash pinchando en su cocina, la rivalidad entre los Cold Crush y los Fantastic Five convertida en partido de baloncesto y batalla, y Grandmaster Caz y sus cuadernos de rimas. El final, un concierto sin permiso en el anfiteatro del East River Park, acabó en «caos de hip hop» con Kool Moe Dee pidiendo saltar. Se estrenó en Japón en 1983 (en Tokio un chaval sin inglés recitaba una cinta de los Cold Crush) y llevó el hip hop al mundo antes que la música, como recordaba Monie Love en Londres; le siguieron Beat Street y Breakin’. Hacia 1988, con Run-DMC, la Costa Oeste y el crack, los pioneros dejaron de recibir llamadas.

refs.q: And it was absolutely hip-hop chaos, which was heaven for the film.
refs.para: So I basically said, “You guys can perform, but we’re not running cameras on you,” which is so fucking cheap and stupid to say. Kool Moe Dee was fuming on stage, and he was watching Busy Bee, and you could see him like, Man, I could crush this guy, with his arms folded. And then it was getting late in the film. You could see that the party was almost over, and he just grabbed a microphone and started pogo-ing across the stage, saying “Jump, jump!” And I think his attitude of like, I’m going to get mine was infectious, because as soon as he started to do that, everyone else poured right out onto the front of the stage to get their attention. And it was absolutely hip-hop chaos, which was heaven for the film.

refs.q: Wild Style is the reason why hip-hop even exists around the planet.
refs.para: DJ Charlie Chase (Cold Crush Brothers): Wild Style is the reason why hip-hop even exists around the planet. That little fuckin’ one-hundred-thousand-dollar bullshit movie right there.

refs.q: The crack epidemic came and pretty much wiped out a lot of us. It took out a whole generation of pioneers.
refs.para: Joe Conzo (photographer): The crack epidemic came and pretty much wiped out a lot of us. It took out a whole generation of pioneers. But most of us bounced back and picked up where we left off.
